context.hint: The decoder now handles named references and decimal or hex numeric references with optional semicolons, and invalid numeric references are left unchanged. The full local suite passes. The remaining closure question is semantic rather than mechanism-level: after sanitization, does any emitted URI attribute re-parse to a blocked scheme when processed by the same HTML parser? A second requirement is packaging: the official patch must contain only the source delta, apply cleanly to a fresh snapshot and reproduce the verified behavior, because tests or run state in the patch would break the host-side evaluation.
context.surface: Python library made of a streaming HTML tokenizer, an attribute policy filter and an entity-preserving serializer. Untrusted markup enters through a sanitize API configured with allowed tags, allowed attributes and allowed URI schemes.
assumptions: The attacker controls the entire untrusted HTML fragment but not the sanitizer configuration or the local filesystem.
Allowed attributes include at least one URI-valued attribute on a link, an image, a video poster, a form action, a cite/background attribute and an SVG link.
The sanitizer's protocol list is configurable; http, https and mailto are allowed by default and a caller may add a custom scheme.
All experiments use a disposable local Python environment and in-memory strings; no network service or public target is involved.
The official benchmark evaluator is external; local test results are not an official pass.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: an attacker can hide a disallowed scheme behind a numeric character reference without a trailing semicolon, which the current decoder leaves intact because it only matches terminated references. Prerequisite: a policy decoder that can consume a maximal digit run. Bounded test: sanitize a link with &#106avascript: plus a plain javascript: control, then also test zero-padded and uppercase-hex variants; record whether the URI attribute remains. Expected result: the repaired decoder consumes decimal or hex digits greedily, optionally consumes one semicolon, resolves the value, and removes the attribute. Falsifier: any no-semicolon form still resolves to a blocked scheme after the repair. Cleanup: revert one helper. Limitations: greedy consumption must not turn a legitimate reference-lookalike into a different scheme.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: a decoder can agree with itself yet still disagree with the renderer, so the only decisive check is to re-parse every emitted URI attribute with the same HTML parser and look for a blocked scheme in the post-parse value. Prerequisite: the same parser used by the sanitizer. Bounded test: sanitize a matrix of attack and control cases, re-parse each emitted attribute once, normalize whitespace/control characters and test the scheme prefix against the allowlist. Expected result: no emitted attack value resolves to a blocked scheme. Falsifier: any surviving javascript: or file: after one parse. Cleanup: keep the matrix script and logs. Limitations: a browser URL parser may differ slightly from the HTML parser.

Hypothesis: aggressive numeric decoding may corrupt legitimate values that merely resemble references, such as a bare ampersand, an AT&T-like query value or an entity-lookalike inside a path. Prerequisite: pristine byte snapshots for those controls. Bounded test: sanitize bare-ampersand, digit-run-in-query and entity-lookalike values before and after the patch and compare bytes. Expected result: all controls are identical. Falsifier: any allowed or relative value changes. Cleanup: discard the fixture. Limitations: some invalid reference forms may legitimately be over-rejected.

Hypothesis: double or nested encoding may survive if the decoder resolves a different number of layers than the browser. Prerequisite: knowledge that the serializer emits one unresolved layer. Bounded test: sanitize one-, two- and three-layer nested references, re-parse the output once, and check the resolved scheme; also inspect raw bytes. Expected result: no first-parse value is a blocked scheme. Falsifier: an emitted value whose first parse yields javascript:. Cleanup: remove the nested cases. Limitations: an external repeated-decoding intermediary could change the result.

Hypothesis: a patch export containing only the source delta will apply cleanly to a fresh snapshot and reproduce the focused and full test results, while test files or run state would cause drift. Prerequisite: a pristine copy and a JSONL with one source-only patch. Bounded test: apply the patch with a patch-check tool, import the fresh copy, rerun the focused and full suites, and compare the matrix output with the working copy. Expected result: clean application and identical tests/output. Falsifier: apply failure, test drift or an extra file in the patch. Cleanup: discard the fresh copy. Limitations: official evaluation is still host-side.

Hypothesis: closure evidence needs one deterministic artifact mapping every attack and control case to its sanitized output, parsed attribute, scheme verdict and pass/fail status, run on both pristine and patched copies. Prerequisite: a consolidated runner keyed by stable case IDs. Bounded test: run the matrix once on pristine and once on patched, assert that attack attributes are gone and control bytes match, then repeat for determinism. Expected result: saved logs show the difference is limited to malicious attributes. Falsifier: any nondeterministic row, surviving attack scheme or control drift. Cleanup: keep both logs as handoff evidence. Limitations: this is verification and packaging, not a new repair mechanism.

evaluations.rationale: Selected incumbent. Strongest saved evidence and the repair to be closed out; the new candidates are verification branches that refine the same mechanism.
Deferred but incorporated. The strongest semantic falsifier: re-parse the emitted value instead of trusting the decoder's internal view.
Deferred but incorporated as controls. Real over-decoding risk, already partly covered by query-ampersand tests.
Deferred. Adds nested-depth coverage without likely changing the repair.
Deferred but required for handoff. Clean-copy application is a mandatory packaging check, not a causal hypothesis.
Deferred but incorporated. Correctly asks for a single deterministic matrix artifact and pristine-versus-patched proof.

observation.summary: Built a consolidated 33-case matrix: 16 attack variants across link, image, video poster, form action, generic background and SVG link attributes, plus 17 allowed, relative, query-ampersand, non-ASCII, malformed, double-encoded and custom-protocol controls. Every case ran the sanitizer and then re-parsed each emitted URI attribute with the same HTML parser before checking the scheme. On the patched copy no attack case retained a URI attribute and no emitted value resolved to a blocked scheme; all 17 controls were byte-identical to the pristine output and none was blocked. Applying only the source-only patch to a fresh snapshot succeeded, the fresh matrix output was identical, and the fresh copy passed the full suite (256 tests, 2 expected failures) plus 22 focused entity-URI checks. The exported JSONL contains one source-only entry. Evidence strength: direct end-to-end local result with a clean-copy replay. Limitation: the official host-side benchmark evaluation was not available and remains unverified.
observation.next_hint: Run the official external evaluator against the supplied patch JSONL and report its verdict separately from these local results.
